questions: Do you have a history of polio?
Is your right leg shorter than your left?
Does your right foot turn inward or downward when you try to walk?
Are you able to lift the front part of your right foot off the ground while sitting?
Can you wiggle the toes on your right foot?
results: 1. slit-lamp examination for Kayser-Fleischer rings: no rings
2. copper / caeruloplasmin / 24 h urinary copper: NORMAL - excludes Wilson disease
3. dystonia gene panel: biallelic GLB1 variants
4. lysosomal enzyme assay (beta-galactosidase, hexosaminidase): REDUCED beta-galactosidase, with 5-10% residual activity - type-III GM1 gangliosidosis
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Type III GM1 gangliosidosis (late-onset juvenile form) caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the GLB1 gene resulting in deficient beta-galactosidase activity.

Alternatives considered:
1. Dopa-responsive dystonia (Segawa syndrome) - often presents with similar lower limb dystonia and foot posturing in childhood, though ruled out by genetic/enzymatic findings.
2. Hereditary spastic paraplegia - can present with leg weakness and gait disturbance, but typically lacks the specific extrapyramidal signs seen here.
dx: Type III GM1 gangliosidosis (late-onset juvenile form) caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the GLB1 gene resulting in deficient beta-galactosidase activity.
